sources.entry: RetroArr ⚠ - Game library manager for PC and retro consoles, with metadata scraping, indexer search, download automation and browser-based emulation (alternative to RomM). (Source Code) MIT Docker/.NET

summary.one_liner: RetroArr is a self-hosted game library manager for PC and retro consoles that scans files, fetches metadata, searches indexers, automates downloads, and offers browser-based emulation, described as "Radarr/Sonarr, but for video games."
summary.what_it_does: It scans a game library and identifies files across 170 platforms, pulling metadata from IGDB (primary), ScreenScraper, Steam, and GOG. It searches indexers (Prowlarr, Jackett, Hydra Launcher, raw Newznab/Torznab) and sends releases to download clients (qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, SABnzbd, NZBGet), then renames and places files by platform. Games or whole platforms can be monitored so a background sweep searches indexers on a schedule and can auto-grab the best-scoring release. It also provides browser-based emulation via EmulatorJS with 23 cores, save states, and BIOS folder handling, plus launch integration for Steam, GOG, and Linux/macOS setups. Storage can be SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MariaDB, and credentials are encrypted with ASP.NET Data Protection.
use_cases: fetch game metadata and cover art automatically
play retro console games in the browser
warm LanCache for Steam, Battle.net, or Epic downloads
monitor games and auto-grab new releases
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the ghcr.io/riddix/retroarr:latest image, ports 2727 (HTTP) and optionally 2728 (HTTPS), and volumes for config, media, and savestates
Open the web UI on port 2727
Go to Settings → Metadata and enter IGDB credentials (Twitch dev account)
notable: Covers PC, retro consoles, handhelds, and arcade platforms in one UI with 170 platform definitions
Monitoring works like Sonarr/Radarr, with scheduled indexer sweeps and optional auto-grab of the best-scoring release
Browser-based emulation through EmulatorJS with 23 cores and 8 save-state slots per game
Security model: API key gate with loopback detection, and short-lived signed links for ROMs and downloads
Desktop builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux alongside the Docker image
caveats: IGDB credentials are required for metadata; the README describes them as free but needs a Twitch developer account
Reverse proxy setups must forward WebSocket upgrades for SignalR, and proxies on the same host must send X-Forwarded-For or their clients are treated as local
Some threaded emulator cores need HTTPS when accessed from a LAN IP
The list entry marks the project with a warning symbol; the README does not explain the reason
